patch_description:
Replace the sampled greedy construction with a deterministic beam search followed by transaction-order local search.

1. The previous method evaluates only a small random subset of remaining transactions at every position. It can therefore discard the transaction whose placement avoids later read/write conflict chains.
2. The new beam search expands several low-cost partial transaction orders simultaneously. Each expansion uses `workload.get_opt_seq_cost`, so ranking is based directly on the actual scheduling makespan rather than transaction length or write counts.
3. Greedy completions from several distinct starting transactions provide additional diverse complete schedules. This avoids beam-search tie breaking concentrating entirely on one early ordering.
4. Each promising complete schedule is improved using best insertion moves. Moving one transaction from one position to another can eliminate long conflict-induced critical paths that cannot be repaired by a purely prefix-greedy method.
5. A cost cache prevents repeated simulator calls for the same order. The search width is bounded by `num_seqs`, keeping the method practical while using substantially more of the available scheduling information than random sampling.
